APCTT-C01.quote: In effect, the diffusivity coefficient incorporates flow resistance and depth into a single calibration.
APCTT-C01.note: Diffusion-analogy basis, contrasted with momentum and mass-conservation models, with citations.

APCTT-C02.quote: The method can be used as a guide to assist in land-use planning and wetland restoration, or to identify and quantify risks to development in or adjacent to the coastal floodplain from future tidal floods or gate failures.
APCTT-C02.note: Practical application for planners and permitting.

APCTT-C03.quote: This simplified, one-dimensional diffusion model was devel-oped, tested, and used to derive tide heights at the boundary of a marsh.
APCTT-C03.note: Calibration results for the four marshes (table 1, p11).

APCTT-C05.quote: On the basis of this validation, the method accu-racy averages about ±0.1 to 0.2 foot with a maximum error of 0.3 foot (the largest error between simulated and observed tide heights).
APCTT-C05.note: Validated against observed tide heights on dates not used for calibration.

APCTT-C06.quote: A geographic information system application of the method is demonstrated for Sybil Creek marsh in Branford, Connecticut.
APCTT-C06.note: Demonstration of the method at a real marsh.

APCTT-C10.note: Accuracy is reported but no requirement is stated.

APCTT-C11.quote: Because of these hydrau-lic issues, the model is calibrated only for the high-tide level of interest.
APCTT-C11.note: Calibration condition (high tide), marshes and data used are defined.

APCTT-C12.quote: A one-dimensional diffusion analogy model for estimating tide heights in coastal marshes was developed and calibrated by using data from previous tidal-marsh studies.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the diffusion-analogy model itself.

notes: Organizer estimate TRL 5; the abstract states a demonstration at Sybil Creek, so this labeller's opinion is TRL 6, low confidence.
